summary: This is a React component that displays code snippets with optional explanations and interactive features. It handles syntax highlighting using Prism, supports line-by-line annotations with tooltips, shows verbose summaries powered by AI, and truncates long code blocks to avoid overwhelming the reader while keeping the full content available to search and screen readers.

explanations.15: This comment explains that certain Prism language grammars (like bash, PHP, etc.) must be imported here because the downstream `Eli5CodeBlock` component needs them available on the shared global Prism object.
explanations.57: React.isValidElement checks if a node is actually a React component (not a string or number), so we can safely access its props.
explanations.62: We're looking for a className attribute that contains the pattern 'language-xyz' (which Prism uses to identify the code language), then extracting just the 'xyz' part with the regex match.
explanations.329: This checks if a character code represents a control character (like ESC or DEL) that would be invalid in HTML—excluding tab, newline, and carriage return which are allowed.
explanations.345: We convert invisible control characters to their Unicode 'control picture' equivalents so they display visibly (like ␛ for ESC) but the actual bytes in the code remain unchanged when copied.
explanations.365: useRef stores a reference to the timeout ID so we can later clear it if needed—useState wouldn't work here because we don't want re-renders when the timeout changes.
explanations.405: We memoize the grammar lookup so Prism doesn't have to search for the language definition on every render; if the language isn't found, we fall back to plaintext or C-like syntax.
explanations.409: useTokenize parses the code through Prism's real token tree instead of just splitting by newlines, which prevents breaking multi-line tokens like block comments across line boundaries.
explanations.415: We check if the last line is a synthetic 'empty' line (Prism adds one if code ends with a newline) and remove it so line numbers stay aligned with the explanation object's keys.
explanations.426: getBoundingClientRect gives us the badge button's screen position so we can position the tooltip directly above it.
explanations.442: We attach scroll and resize listeners so the tooltip stays glued to its badge button—without this, scrolling would leave the tooltip stranded at its old screen position.
explanations.445: The capture: true flag means we listen during the capturing phase (before bubbling), and passive: true tells the browser this listener won't call preventDefault, letting it optimize scrolling performance.
explanations.496: This callback ref updates our badgeRefs map whenever a badge button mounts or unmounts, so we can later look up its DOM position by line number.
explanations.508: onMouseEnter and onMouseLeave update the tooltip position and visibility—we position it first, then set the active line to trigger a render that shows the tooltip.
explanations.530: We only render the tooltip into document.body via a Portal if mounted is true, because during server-side rendering document.body doesn't exist and createPortal would fail.
explanations.561: useId generates a unique string per component instance so the contentId is stable across renders and properly links the button to the content div via aria-controls.
explanations.565: We measure the content's actual height (scrollHeight) and update the CSS max-height—this animates the disclosure open/closed while keeping the content reachable by find-in-page.
explanations.587: We conditionally add the 'rotate' class to the chevron so it rotates 180° when open, giving visual feedback that the section is expanded.
explanations.665: We remove trailing newlines before splitting so the line count matches what the user sees—a trailing newline would create a fake empty line 31 after a 30-line file.
explanations.689: defaultOpen ?? true means 'if defaultOpen was explicitly passed, use that value; otherwise default to true', making snippets open by default unless the caller says otherwise.
explanations.706: We extract the file extension by splitting on dots and taking the last piece, then look it up in mapLangToVariant to convert something like 'py' into the variant key 'python'.
explanations.718: useVarResolver returns a function that substitutes variable markers like '%%varname=default%%' with actual values, letting readers customize code snippets.
explanations.725: We map over children (which might contain variable markers) and wrap substituted values in VarToken components that show them with a visual underline.
explanations.739: We pick the Eli5CodeBlock renderer if there are line-by-line explanations or if the code contains invisible control characters (which only Eli5CodeBlock can display safely while preserving copy behavior).
explanations.751: We extract just the filename (everything after the last slash) and lowercase it for comparison, since 'dockerfile' can appear as './Dockerfile' or other case variants.
explanations.792: peeking is true when the file is long, the user has opened it, but hasn't clicked 'show all lines' yet—at this point we show only the first PEEK_LINES lines with a fade.
